headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Plane can handle files and broad egress while Superset has allowlisted egress, but no direct shared-channel evidence makes prompt-injection and conflict lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane can ingest file uploads and notes, and Superset exposes a Superset API, so a manual or file-based bridge could carry malicious instructions. However, no shared filesystem, clipboard, or direct parser coupling is documented, so the pathway is not default. The interaction is inferred from both profiles, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF an operator copies Plane content into Superset inputs without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace or message bridge is added, attacker-controlled content can cross agents.
mitigations: Use copy/paste only for plain text and strip markup.
Add a human review step before any Superset action.
Disable any shared folder or sync bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches files, images, hyperlinks, and notes and has broad network egress; Superset has allowlisted egress. If Plane content includes sensitive work items, moving it into Superset can expose that data to another service path. No direct shared workspace is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed, but the default data-handling surface is broad enough to warrant medium severity.
conditions: IF Plane tasks or uploaded files contain sensitive data and are forwarded into Superset, leakage risk exists.
IF Superset is configured to query external sources using Plane-derived content, that content may leave the original boundary.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in Plane tasks or uploads.
Redact sensitive fields before exporting to Superset.
Restrict Superset datasets to non-sensitive sources.
Review outbound destinations in both systems.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on cross-system transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane cannot write the filesystem and only supports multiple instances; Superset exposes only the Superset API and allowlisted egress. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource documented, direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because the profiles do not describe orchestration locks, so I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API object, write contention can occur.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto one mutable dataset, conflicts may appear.
mitigations: Assign separate datasets or projects.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same external resource.
Schedule edits sequentially.
Check for duplicate updates after sync.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can produce issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, and notes that Superset could consume as analytical input. Superset is not documented as verifying those inputs before use, so erroneous Plane output could cascade into dashboards or decisions. Because the handoff is inferred and not directly documented, medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Superset dashboards or queries are built from Plane-exported content, errors can propagate.
IF operators treat Plane-generated records as authoritative without review, downstream analysis may be wrong.
mitigations: Require manual validation of Plane exports.
Label imported fields as untrusted.
Compare key metrics against source systems.
Limit automated refreshes from Plane-derived inputs.
requires-engineering: add schema and quality checks before ingestion.

E_compliance.rationale: Plane explicitly touches files and notes and offers self-hosted deployment, while Superset is an analytics platform with allowlisted egress. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so a compliance breach is not established. The main issue is that cross-system handling of regulated data could create gaps if configured that way.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Plane and then analyzed in Superset under different retention rules, a policy mismatch can arise.
IF either deployment is hosted in a restricted jurisdiction and the other is not, residency controls may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both systems.
Document retention settings for each system.
Align hosting regions before syncing data.
Review access logs weekly.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement.
